product: Privileged Remote Access and Remote Support
author: Aaronjacobs000
notes: BeyondTrust Privileged Remote Access and Remote Support appliances write the same syslog format: a BG header with a site ID and segment numbers, then field=value pairs separated by semicolons. Send it from /appliance > Security > Appliance Administration > Syslog to the data collector. Logins (with the failure reason), access console logouts and password changes go to Auth; every other event (users, settings, policies, vault accounts and password rotations) goes to ManagementEvent with the whole field list in operation. A line doesn't say whether PRA or RS sent it. Messages over 1 KB arrive as segments and stay in the generic schema. Session activity (session start and end, file transfer, shell) isn't in the appliance syslog; BeyondTrust sends it through its Middleware Engine SIEM Tool plugin, which this entry doesn't cover. Samples follow the examples on BeyondTrust's message format pages with made-up values. Each child, combined with the parent into one parser, passed Run Test in a lab tenant on 2026-10-14 (116 of 116 fields matched the emulator, including a value with an escaped semicolon and the three header variants), and the parent's confirm string picked the same lines there. Each child also passed Run Test as a separate parser under its parent. No built-in parser claimed these lines in 9 Run Tests. BeyondTrust doesn't quote values, so the parent gives SPLIT_NAME_VALUES the backslash, which BeyondTrust escapes, as the quote character. With " as the quote character, a lone " in a value, such as 27" in a display name, made the studio's emulator join the fields after it, which Sophos NG-SIEM doesn't. In Run Test on 2026-10-16 all 130 fields matched the emulator, a quoted value with an escaped = included.
